title: Trend Following...Austrian Style - Open Interest 8

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Trend Following...Austrian Style - Open Interest 8.docx

speakers: Joseph valin (SMN head of quant research and risk)
summary: Austrian CTA SMN (27-year track record) describes agnostic medium/long-term trend following over 200 markets incl. exotic and synthetic ones. Dispersion among CTAs comes from universe and position sizing more than signals. Conclusion: stay symmetric long/short, avoid overfitting, diversify into low-liquidity markets after realistic costs.

coverage.note: background, SMN origin story, no method content
origin of firm, hybrid discretion experiment mention
discretion experiment failed, sources of dispersion
biased signals, symmetric long/short, risk definition start
research of illiquid markets, slippage, alpha
execution algos, synthetic markets, equity ideas
VIX handling, future of trend following
outliers cannot be arbitraged, lost decade, close

completeness_estimate: 0.90 - the first reader caught nearly every method and mechanism claim; only the robustness rationale for choosing trend following, the capacity argument, the sector/single-name equity idea and the volatility-is-non-directional rationale were missed.

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: there's only one assumption behind the concepts and this assumption is a broadly Diversified portfolio will have a certain amount of train outliers over time
claims.claim: Trend following needs no forecast; it only assumes that a broad portfolio will contain some large trend outliers over time, so direction and timing of the next one need not be known.
claims.testable: partly - outlier frequency can be measured but is the assumption itself

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: this would have been a style shift and this is something you should never do
claims.claim: Adding discretionary overlays was tested only in a side fund, never in the flagship, because changing style in a live track record is to be avoided; the discretionary plus systematic mix failed.
claims.testable: no - governance statement

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: the Universe and the position sizing logic they have more weight in differentiation than the third
claims.claim: Dispersion among trend-following CTAs is explained more by market universe and position-sizing logic than by signal design.
claims.testable: partly - could be tested with CTA fund data

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: constant versus flexible risk targeting is one big issue
claims.claim: Position sizing choices that differ across managers include constant versus flexible risk targeting and whether sizing uses only signal direction or the signal value.
claims.testable: yes - alternative sizing rules can be backtested

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: giving more weight to long where the short signals for instance in the fixed income world or in the equity world
claims.claim: Some CTAs bias signals toward long positions in bonds and equities, which is another source of dispersion in trend following results.
claims.testable: yes - long-only versus symmetric tilt can be backtested

claims.speaker: Moritz seibert
claims.quote: the long- sided trades and equities and bonds have been performing so much better than the shortsighted trades
claims.claim: Over the last 30-40 years long trades in equity and bond trend following beat short trades, while currencies and commodities show a different pattern; this is a sample-specific effect of secular bull markets.
claims.direction: long equities and bonds outperformed short
claims.testable: yes - split trend returns by long and short side

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: we try not to over optimize and and and this this is really dangerous because what works in the past probably doesn't work in the future
claims.claim: Tilting signals to what worked in the past (for example removing short signals) is overfitting; SMN keeps equal risk on long and short signals in every market.
claims.testable: partly - cannot prove out of sample absence of change

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: this year the best Market in a uh CTA portfolio was uh the market Coco this is a market that was produced more or less always negative returns over time
claims.claim: Cocoa, historically a negative-return trend market, was the best CTA market in 2024, showing that the location of the next outlier cannot be predicted from history.
claims.testable: partly - single anecdote

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: one of the characteristics of of ctas is that they are able to produce the the crisis alha
claims.claim: Removing short signals would improve a backtest during 30 years of bull markets in bonds and equities but would destroy the crisis alpha that trend following is expected to deliver.
claims.direction: keep shorts in equities and bonds
claims.testable: yes - compare long-only and long/short trend in drawdowns

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: we do not Target the overall um risk goal in terms of an deviation goal on a daily basis just on average long-term Bas
claims.claim: Volatility target is an annualised standard deviation goal met on average over the long run; the portfolio is not re-levered on days with few signals.
claims.testable: yes - compare constant versus flexible risk targeting

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: we have assigned stop loss limits for each or risk budgets for each position we're trading for each signal we are trading
claims.claim: Each position has a risk budget or stop limit to control drawdown, complementing the symmetric standard deviation target with an asymmetric drawdown control.
claims.testable: yes - position-level stop rule can be backtested

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: the systems react on these developments by U reducing position uh the position size in case of a huge development in in individual price development
claims.claim: When a market makes a huge move (cocoa) and the exit level lags far below price, positions are cut so one market does not dominate; limits are deliberately broad so ordinary moves do not trigger cuts.
claims.indicator: distance from price to exit level, price volatility
claims.conditions: only after very large individual price moves
claims.testable: yes - rule can be backtested

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: from the very beginning it was very important for us to diversify the risk by markets
claims.claim: More markets give more chances to catch outlier moves, so SMN began with about 70 markets and kept widening the universe.
claims.testable: yes - breadth versus Sharpe in backtests

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: if we can produce a curve with uh two that looks different with two other curves then we would get more diversification
claims.claim: Synthetic markets built as baskets or spreads of existing markets create return streams that look different from the underlying and add diversification.
claims.testable: yes - build spreads and measure incremental diversification

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: only concentrate on medium to long term because we thought this is the this is the uh the thing that is most robust over time
claims.claim: SMN dropped short-term systems around 2007-08 and concentrated on medium/long-term trend following as the most robust horizon.
claims.testable: partly - robustness is judgement

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: investors because of the liquidity of CTS uh took out money because they needed it as well
claims.claim: In the 2008 crisis CTAs did well but investors redeemed from them because CTAs were liquid, so crisis alpha did not bring new assets.
claims.testable: no - anecdote

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: the career risk for them when they lose money with them is lower
claims.claim: Allocators prefer the biggest CTA shops because of career risk, so small firms can differentiate only by trading markets large funds cannot.
claims.testable: no - industry structure view

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: it's not this typical risk on riskof regime that you have with most of the high highest liquid financial and commodity markets they have their own moves and they don't correlate too much to the rest of the portfolio
claims.claim: Alternative (illiquid, regional) markets move on local factors rather than the global risk-on/risk-off regime, so they correlate little with a classic futures portfolio.
claims.indicator: correlation of alternative markets with classic portfolio
claims.testable: yes - correlation and Sharpe contribution measurable

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: we came up with really huge reasonable but still obviously much more higher slippage numbers incorporating our P testing
claims.claim: Backtests of illiquid markets use deliberately high slippage assumptions, plus broker execution costs, to avoid overstating results.
claims.conditions: slippage hard to know ex ante for illiquid markets
claims.testable: yes - cost stress in backtests

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: even after accounting for this High number of slippage and transaction costs explicit and implicit transaction cost there is sizable Alpha to capture
claims.claim: After stringent cost assumptions, adding less liquid markets still raises the portfolio Sharpe ratio significantly.
claims.indicator: portfolio Sharpe ratio with and without alternative markets
claims.testable: yes - incremental Sharpe test with cost stress

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: the pricing behavior in these less liquid markets is more cycle driven driven because in our case predominantly but not only but PR predominantly commodity markets local commodity markets more driven by local demand and Supply
claims.claim: Local commodity markets driven by local supply and demand show medium to long-term price cycles that trend systems capture well.
claims.testable: yes - trend profitability by market type

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: these Trends do not happen at the same time than with our classic universe meaning decreasing correlation and increasing diversification
claims.claim: Trends in alternative markets occur at different times from classic-market trends, lowering correlation and improving diversification.
claims.testable: yes - correlation of trend returns

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: the biggest enemy in researching is that the over optimization of the past
claims.claim: SMN has standard rules to judge whether a backtest result is realistic because over-optimisation of the past is the main research risk.
claims.testable: partly - rules not stated

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: I would assume right now it's really I think uh four to five times larger than the the classical ones
claims.claim: Slippage assumed for the smallest markets (nonfat dry milk, cheese) is roughly four to five times that of classic futures.
claims.testable: partly - estimate stated from memory

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: so in these markets we U decided to trade them with with Algos together with our Brokers
claims.claim: Tiny illiquid markets are traded with execution algorithms (TWAP or similar) over a day or two to spread liquidity, with instructions per market.
claims.conditions: illiquid markets, positions need more than one session
claims.testable: no - execution practice

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: risk parity baskets it's a it's basically a combination between an equity
claims.claim: The first synthetic markets (2009) were risk-parity baskets of an equity index and a government bond, for example S&P versus 10-year note.
claims.testable: yes - basket trend backtest

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: a correlation spread we where we trade um two related Commodities like Coco versus London cocoa or different wheat wheat types
claims.claim: Correlation spreads between related commodities (New York versus London cocoa, wheat types) are traded as synthetic markets with their own trends; synthetics are roughly 20-25% of risk.
claims.testable: yes - spread trend backtest

correction.issue: The 20-25% of risk figure for synthetic markets was read out by the host (Moritz, citing a Hedge Fund Journal article), not stated by Joseph; SMN did not confirm the number.
correction.fix: Correlation spreads between related commodities (New York versus London cocoa, wheat types, South African maize and soybeans) are traded as synthetic markets with their own trends; the host cites an article putting synthetics at about 20-25% of SMN's risk budget.

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: you could for example make a spread out of uh an equally uh weighted stock index versus uh volume weighted uh stock index
claims.claim: An equal-weighted versus cap-weighted stock index spread could provide a trend market, with an eventual trend outlier in the other direction after the Magnificent Seven run.
claims.testable: yes - spread trend backtest

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: the behavior of the especially asset class volatility in our case you Equity volatility the behavior was not the most optimal one for the way we traded the other markets
claims.claim: Pure momentum on the VIX behaved poorly in the 2009-2019 lost decade, so SMN built an enhanced momentum model.
claims.testable: yes - compare pure and enhanced VIX momentum

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: we take into account next to the price movement of volatility so the volatility of volatility actually also the shape of future and expected the the uh state of spot and future volatility
claims.claim: Enhanced VIX momentum uses price momentum, the volatility of volatility and the shape of the futures curve (spot versus future volatility).
claims.indicator: VIX futures price, vol of vol, term-structure shape
claims.testable: yes - rule can be replicated

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: we're moved to basically hourly hourly ticks in order to evaluate the the structure of the the current structure of the volatility
claims.claim: VIX positions are monitored on hourly snapshots of the curve with quick intraday exits because volatility can explode.
claims.testable: yes - needs intraday data

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: when you have uh a couple of good years then investors think probably it's a good idea to have a small proportionate portfolios with CTS as well
claims.claim: Allocator interest in CTAs follows recent performance: after drawdowns investors say trend following no longer works, after good years they add, a pattern unchanged for 30 years.
claims.testable: partly - flows versus performance data

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: arbitraging away this big outliers is impossible because there are other reasons for this then CTA trades
claims.claim: Trend following is unlikely to be arbitraged away because large outliers have causes other than CTA trading, though more noise could create more false signals.
claims.testable: no - future-looking claim

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: if it takes for a long time if the markets have for a long time no substantial moves then they are prepared having even bigger moves than uh on average after this period
claims.claim: The 2009-2020 lost decade (zero rates, QE) had few outliers, was artificial, and long quiet periods are followed by bigger-than-average moves, as seen now.
claims.testable: partly - few historical episodes

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: it was the the concept that we where we found the highest robustness
claims.claim: SMN chose trend following (after testing technical indicators on the bank desk) because it was the concept it found most robust, with the Turtles' and local CTAs' success as extra motivation.
claims.direction: trend following over other technical approaches
claims.testable: no - biographical rationale, not independently testable

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: you can say you trade those markets but uh it doesn't have an effect on the outcome of the portfolio of performance wise
claims.claim: Alpha in small alternative markets is capacity-limited: a multi-billion fund can trade them but the allocation is too small to move performance, so only a mid-sized CTA like SMN can use them as a real source of return.
claims.direction: alternative markets add return mainly for smaller funds
claims.conditions: needs assets small relative to market liquidity
claims.testable: partly - capacity versus return analysis needs fund-level data

claims.speaker: Michael nobow
claims.quote: I think there would be a lot of possibilities for higher diversification as well in in our fund
claims.claim: Breaking equity index futures into sectors or single names would add diversification to a trend portfolio, but SMN has not done it because it would need derivatives (counterparty risk) or a change of the fund prospectus.
claims.direction: more diversification from sector/single-name trend markets
claims.testable: partly - needs stock-level data, not tested in the talk

claims.speaker: Joseph valin
claims.quote: the ESS class volatility is really different to all the other more directional ESS classes
claims.claim: Volatility is a non-directional asset class, so SMN argues it needs its own signal design rather than the plain price-momentum rule used for the directional markets.
claims.conditions: VIX trend rule differs from rest of portfolio
claims.testable: partly - compare pure vs enhanced momentum on VIX
